Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 66, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat al-Tahrim

It is Madani.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the pleasure of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ There are two well-known opinions concerning this verse. The more apparent of the two opinions is that it was revealed concerning the Messenger of Allah's prohibiting upon himself Mariyah the Copt. The cause of this was that the Prophet was alone with her in the house of Hafsah, and Hafsah had gone out to visit her father. When she returned and learned of this, she stood at the door, and the Prophet came out and saw the sadness in her face. In another report, she argued with him somewhat about this and said, "This is because of my lowliness in your sight and the smallness of my standing; had it been in the house of someone other than me, you would not have done this." So he prohibited Mariyah upon himself, seeking her pleasure, and he said to her, "Do not inform Aisha of this."

The second opinion: the Prophet used to drink honey in the house of Zaynab bint Jahsh. In another report, in the house of Sawdah, and in another report, in the house of Umm Salamah. So Aisha and Hafsah conspired that whenever the Prophet entered upon either of them, whichever one it was would say, "I smell maghafir on you." It has been reported that Safiyyah was also with them in this conspiracy. So the Prophet entered upon Aisha and she said that to him, and he entered upon Hafsah and she said that to him, and he entered upon Safiyyah and she said that to him. The Prophet disliked that any odor be found on him because of the angels. So he said, "I drank honey at Zaynab's." They said to him, "A nahlah has grazed on the 'arfaṭ," and 'arfaṭ is a tree from which a smell is found. ﴿Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾. Then he prohibited honey upon himself, and said, "I will never return to drinking it." This opinion was related by Ubayd ibn Umayr from Aisha. The first opinion is the view of Umar, Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, and the majority of the exegetes.

It is also reported from Ibn Abbas in one narration that the verse was revealed concerning a woman who offered herself in marriage to the Prophet, but this is an anomalous (shadh) opinion. The meaning of the verse is a rebuke addressed to the Prophet for prohibiting what Allah made lawful for him, seeking the pleasure of his wives.

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, we have already explained it.

The words of Almighty Allah: ﴿Indeed, Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾. That is, the expiation (kaffarah) of your oaths. The word "fard" (ordained) here carries the sense of "clarification" (bayan) and "designation" (tasmiyah). It is also said to carry the sense of "determination" (taqdir), because the expiations are determined and enumerated.

If it is asked: where is the oath in the verse, when Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾? The answer has two aspects:

The first: the Prophet (ﷺ) had forbidden something and swore an oath, and so he was rebuked for the prohibition and was commanded to reflect on the oath. This is a view transmitted from a group of the Followers (tabi'un), among them Masruq and al-Sha'bi and others.

The second aspect: he had forbidden something without swearing an oath, but the forbidding of what is lawful (tahrim al-halal) necessitates an expiation. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas and others.

The scholars differed concerning the forbidding of what is lawful (tahrim al-halal). Ibn Mas'ud held that whoever forbids any lawful thing whatsoever, an expiation is incumbent upon him. This is the view of a group of the Followers, and it is the view of Sufyan al-Thawri and the Kufans. As for the position of Malik and al-Shafi'i, the forbidding of what is lawful regarding women necessitates an expiation, but regarding other than women it necessitates nothing. A group held that the forbidding of what is lawful is nothing at all. Masruq said: "I do not care whether my wife is forbidden to me or a bowl of thareed," meaning that it is nothing. It is reported from some of them that it is an oath of abstention (ila'). It is reported from some of them that it is a zihar. It is reported from some of them that it obliges the triple divorce by forbidding what is lawful regarding women. It is reported from some of them that it depends on his intention.

The "tahillat al-yamin" (dissolution of the oath) is the expiation of the oath, and it was named tahillah because one is released (yatahallal) by it from the oath, that is, one exits it. It is reported from some of them that the tahillat al-yamin is the exception (istithna'), because one exits the oath by means of it. The first is the well-known view. The explanation of the expiation is in Surah al-Ma'idah in the words of Almighty Allah: ﴿But He will hold you accountable for the oaths you have sworn deliberately﴾, the verse. It is related that the Prophet (ﷺ) freed a slave.

As for His words: ﴿And Allah is your Protector (mawlakum)﴾, that is, the Guardian of your affairs, guiding you to what is more right, more upright and more fitting.

As for His words: ﴿And He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise﴾, that is, the Knower of the affairs of His creation, the Wise in what He arranges for them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 66, verse 3:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And when the Prophet confided a matter to one of his wives, a statement﴾. She is Hafsah, may Allah be pleased with her, and what he confided to her was his prohibition of Mariyah. Maymun ibn Mihran said: He confided this to her, and he also confided to her that the caliphate after him would belong to Abu Bakr, and then to her father after him. This is mentioned in many tafsir works from Maymun ibn Mihran and others.

His words: ﴿But when she informed of it﴾. It is narrated that the Prophet said to Hafsah: "Do not tell anyone about this." She did not keep anything secret from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, so she went and informed Aishah of it. Then Jibril descended and informed him of what had passed between them, and this is His words: ﴿And Allah made it known to him﴾.

His words: ﴿He made known part of it﴾, that is, he made her aware of some of what had passed between them, and he turned away from part of it out of generosity and forgiveness. Overlooking many matters is the disposition of the wise and of the noble. It is said: The intelligent are the ones who feign ignorance. What he made known to her was his informing her of the prohibition of Mariyah, and what he turned away from was the matter of Abu Bakr and Umar, out of generosity, so that it would not spread among the people. Al-Kisa'i read ﴿عرف بعضه﴾ (ʿarrafa baʿḍahu) with light emphasis (takhfif). Al-Farra' said: That is, he requited her for it, and his requital of her was that he divorced her; then Jibril descended and commanded him to take her back, and said: "She is fasting often and standing in prayer often." Al-Farra' also said: This is like the saying of one person to another: "I will surely know what you have done," meaning: "I will surely requite you for it." It is also like the words of the Exalted: ﴿And We revealed to him that you will surely inform them of this matter﴾, meaning: you will surely requite them.

His words: ﴿And he turned away from part﴾, that is, he did not requite her for it.

His words: ﴿So when he informed her of it﴾, that is, he told her.

His words: ﴿She said: Who informed you of this?﴾, that is, who told you of this?

His words: ﴿He said: The All-Knowing, the All-Aware informed me﴾, that is, Allah, for He is the All-Knowing of matters, the All-Aware of what is in the breasts.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 66, verse 4:

And His saying, Most High: ﴿If you two repent to Allah﴾. This is an address to ʿĀ'isha and Ḥafṣa, and its meaning is: if you two repent, then you have already done what is incumbent upon you in that regard, namely repentance. What the two of them had done was: backing one another against the Prophet by collusion, as we have explained, and by being pleased at what displeased him, namely the prohibition of what Allah had made lawful for him, and by their intense jealousy over him and by harming him thereby.

And His saying: ﴿then your hearts have inclined﴾, meaning: your hearts have swerved from what is right. It has been narrated that he would tilt (yuṣghī) the vessel for the cat, meaning he would incline it.

And His saying: ﴿your hearts﴾, meaning: your two hearts. Al-Farrāʾ said: this is like the Arabs' saying: "We struck your backs and smashed your heads," meaning your two heads and your two backs. It is said that most of the body's organs come in pairs, and when they are mentioned by the plural form, what is singular follows the same pattern, such as "the head" and "the heart" and other things. This was mentioned by al-Naqqāsh.

And His saying: ﴿And if you two back one another against him﴾. It is established that Ibn ʿAbbās asked ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, about the two women who backed one another against the Prophet, meaning they agreed upon doing what would grieve him and harm him, and others would be against him. He said: they are Ḥafṣa and ʿĀ'isha.

And His saying: ﴿then indeed Allah is his Protector﴾, meaning: his Helper and Guardian. ﴿And Gabriel﴾, meaning: he too will help and protect him.

And His saying: ﴿and the righteous of the believers﴾. Regarding this there are several opinions. The first: al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Ziyād said: they are the Prophets, and this is the view of Qatāda in one of the two narrations, and it is the view of Sufyān al-Thawrī.

It is related from Qatāda in another narration that he said: it is Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, and they are the fathers of the two women. Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūba, who was transmitting this from Qatāda, said: I mentioned that to Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and he said: Qatāda has spoken truly. Al-Layth narrated from Mujāhid that he said: it is ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him. And from some of them: it is the best of the believers.

And His saying: ﴿and the angels after that are a supporting company﴾, meaning: helpers and assistants. (Ẓahīr) is singular in meaning but used for the plural, like His saying, Most High: ﴿And excellent are those as companions (rafīqan)﴾, meaning companions (rufaqāʾ). The poet said:

(Indeed the blamers have no authority over me ...)

meaning: no commanders (umarāʾ). It is narrated that ʿUmar rebuked Ḥafṣa and said: If the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had commanded me to strike your neck, I would have struck it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 66, verse 5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you⦆. If it is asked: how can they be "better than you" when at that time there was no woman better than them? The answer: its meaning is, if he divorces you by your compelling him to divorce, and your great harm to him, and your refusal to repent, then He will substitute for him one better than you, i.e., more obedient to him than you, and it is said: more beloved to him than you.

His saying: ﴿Muslimat﴾ means: submissive, compliant.

His saying: ﴿Mu'minat﴾ means: affirming (in belief).

His saying: ﴿Qanitat﴾ means: obedient.

His saying: ﴿Ta'ibat﴾ means: repentant from all sins, and from everything that harms the Prophet.

His saying: ﴿'Abidat﴾ means: humble, or performing acts of worship as Allah, may He be exalted, has commanded them.

His saying: ﴿Sa'ihat﴾ means: fasting. Ibn Qutaybah said: the fasting person was called "sa'ih" (one who travels) because the traveler (sa'ih) journeys without provision, and if he finds something he eats it in extreme hunger. It is also said: "sa'ihat" means: emigrating (muhajirat).

His saying: ﴿Thayyibat wa abkara﴾: the meaning is apparent. It is also said: the thayyib (previously married) is like Asiya, and the abkar (virgins) are like Maryam, peace be upon them both.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 66, verse 6:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire﴾. That is: by your doing the obedience of Allah, and by your commanding them to obey Allah. It is also said: discipline them, teach them, and guide them to good. In some of the strange reports it is related: "Hang the whip where your family can see it," meaning: for discipline. And on the authority of Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i, who said: "Indeed a woman will dispute with her husband on the Day of Resurrection before Allah, and she will say: 'He did not discipline me, and he did not teach me anything; he would bring me bread from the market.'" It is also said: "Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire" means: protect yourselves from a Fire and protect your families from a Fire by what we have mentioned, and this is the estimated sense of the verse.

And His saying: ﴿Its fuel is people and stones﴾. We have already explained this in Surat al-Baqarah; it is stones of sulphur (al-kibrit).

And His saying: ﴿Over it are angels, harsh and severe﴾. That is: harsh of heart, severe of hand. In the tafsir it is related that one of them throws seventy thousand in a single push into the Fire. In some of the reports: "Indeed Allah, exalted is He, has not placed in the hearts of the guardians (al-zabaniyah) any mercy at all." And on the authority of some of them: he seizes the disbelieving servant with fierce violence, and that servant says: "Will you not have mercy on me?" He says: "How can I have mercy on you, when the Most Merciful of the merciful has not had mercy on you?"

And in some reports also: Allah, exalted is He, becomes angry with one of His servants, and says to the angels: "Seize him." Then a hundred thousand angels rush to him, all of them angry with the anger of Allah, exalted is He, and they drag him to the Fire, and the Fire is angrier with him than they are by seventy times.

And His saying: ﴿They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded﴾. Its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 66, verse 7:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have disbelieved, do not make excuses today﴾. He means: it will be said to them on the Day of Resurrection, "Do not make excuses," i.e., you have no excuse, so that you could make one.

And His saying: ﴿You are only being recompensed for what you used to do﴾, i.e., for your deeds in the worldly life.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 66, verse 8:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed﴾. Al-Zuhri said: "Every place in the Qur'an that says ﴿O you who have believed﴾ followed by a command ('do such-and-such'), the Prophet ﷺ is included among them." It is related from Khaythama that he said: "Everything in the Qur'an that says ﴿O you who have believed﴾ is in the Torah as 'O you who are humble (al-masakin)'." We have already mentioned from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "When you hear God say ﴿O you who have believed﴾, give it your full hearing, for it is something you are being commanded to do, or something you are being forbidden from."

﴿O you who have believed, repent to God with sincere repentance (tawbatan nasuha). Perhaps your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow, on the Day when God will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him. Their light will run before them and on their right hands; they will say, "Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed You are over all things competent."﴾

As for His saying: ﴿repent to God with sincere repentance﴾, Umar and Ibn Mas'ud said: it is that one repents from a sin and then never returns to it ever again. It is also said: nasuha means truthful (sadiqa), and it is said: pure (khalisa), and it is said: firm and reliable (muhkama wathiqa). It is derived from nasah, which is sewing (al-khiyata), as if repentance mends the tear of sin so that it is joined together, like a tailor who sews with a thread so that it is joined. It has also been recited "nusuhan" with a damma on the nun, meaning "possessing sincerity (dhat nush)."

As for His saying: ﴿Perhaps your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds﴾, we have already explained that "perhaps" (asa) from God is binding.

As for His saying: ﴿and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾, that is, orchards (basatin).

As for His saying: ﴿on the Day when God will not disgrace the Prophet﴾, that is, He will not humiliate or expose him. This is an indication of honour in the Hereafter; that is, He will honour and ennoble him on that Day, and will not humiliate or abase him.

As for His saying: ﴿and those who believed with him﴾, that is, likewise He will do so for those who believed with him.

As for His saying: ﴿Their light will run before them﴾, it is the light of faith, which will be before them on the Sirat, and they will walk by its illumination. It is mentioned in the tafsir that each one of them will have a light like a mountain, and another will have a light the size of his toenail, which goes out at times and flares up at others.

As for His saying: ﴿and on their right hands﴾, there are two opinions regarding it: the first is that it means their books (kutubuhum) on their right hands; the second is that it means their light on their right hands, like lamps.

As for His saying: ﴿they will say, "Our Lord, perfect for us our light"﴾, it is mentioned in the [tafsir] that they will say this when the light of the hypocrites is extinguished and goes out, so they say this out of concern for their own light.

As for His saying: ﴿and forgive us. Indeed You are over all things competent﴾, that is, Capable (qadir).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 66, verse 9:

The Most High's saying: ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers﴾, i.e., with the sword.

And His saying: ﴿and the hypocrites﴾, i.e., with the tongue. It is also said: with harshness toward them. Ibn Mas'ud said: that he should meet them with a scowling face. It is also said: by enforcing the prescribed punishments upon them; this was mentioned by a group of the Followers (tabi'un).

And His saying: ﴿and be harsh with them. Their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination﴾, i.e., the place of return.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 66, verse 10:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿God presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot﴾. In some exegeses it is said that the name of one of them was Wahila, and the other was Wali'a.

His saying: ﴿They were under two of Our righteous servants﴾, meaning Noah and Lot, peace be upon them both.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿but they betrayed them﴾. Opinions differ regarding this. One opinion is that the betrayal was by disbelief.

The second opinion is that the betrayal was by hypocrisy: they would show faith and conceal disbelief.

The third opinion is that it was by slander (namimah).

The fourth opinion concerns the madness attributed to Noah and the guiding of guests to Lot. Noah's wife would say to anyone who came seeking Noah, so that he would hear, "He is mad." Lot's wife would direct her people to Lot's guests for the purpose of indecency. It is related in the narrative that during the day she would send signals, and at night she would light smoke and kindle a fire so that they would know. Ibn 'Abbas said: "No wife of a prophet ever committed adultery (baghat)", meaning she never committed fornication.

His saying: ﴿but they did not avail them against God in anything﴾, meaning Noah and Lot could not ward off (yadfa'a) from them, that is, from their wives, anything. The intended meaning is a warning to 'A'isha and Hafsa, namely: if you disobey your Lord, the Messenger of God will not avail you in anything, just as Noah and Lot did not avail their wives.

His saying: ﴿And it was said: "Enter the Fire with those who enter."﴾, meaning it was said to the two women.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 66, verse 11:

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And Allah presents an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh﴾. She is Asiya bint Muzahim. She had believed in Allah and in Musa, peace be upon him, secretly, then made it apparent. Pharaoh tortured her and punished her. And in the narrative: he staked her out with four stakes of iron. And in the narrative: the first woman to believe was the treasurer's wife of Pharaoh, and it is said: the hairdresser (mashita) of Pharaoh's daughter. Pharaoh tortured her and she endured that patiently, so Asiya then made her faith apparent.

And His saying: ﴿When she said: My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise﴾, meaning: a dwelling.

And His saying: ﴿And save me from Pharaoh and his deeds﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions: one of them is: from his polytheism; the other is: from lying with him (al-mudaja'a ma'ahu, i.e., sexual intercourse). And it is said: from intercourse (al-jima').

And His saying: ﴿And save me from the wrongdoing people﴾, meaning: from the people of Pharaoh.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 66, verse 12:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Mary, daughter of 'Imran, who guarded her chastity﴾. The more widely held of the two views is that it refers to the private part itself. The Arabs say: "So-and-so guarded her chastity (aḥṣanat farjahā)" when she abstained from fornication.

The second view is that the farj (private part) here is the collar (al-jayb, the neckline of a garment). Al-Farra' said: every tear in a shirt or anything else is a farj. It is also said that in the recitation of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "So We blew into her collar (jaybihā) of Our spirit."

As for His saying in the story: ﴿So We breathed into it of Our spirit﴾, the account is that Jibril, peace be upon him, blew into the collar of her garment, and so she conceived 'Isa. It is narrated that he came to her in the form of a beardless young man with curly hair, while she was wearing a woollen garment. Abu Mu'adh al-Nahwi said: "in her woollen garment." According to the first view, if we say that it is the private part itself, then the blowing into the collar of her garment becomes like blowing into her private part itself.

His saying: ﴿And she confirmed the words of her Lord﴾. It was recited also as: "the word of her Lord." The meaning of "the words" is what Allah, may He be exalted, informed of as glad tidings concerning 'Isa, his description, his honour with Allah, and other matters. It is also said: "the words of her Lord" means "the signs of her Lord." As for His saying: ﴿the word of her Lord﴾, it refers to 'Isa, peace be upon him.

His saying: ﴿and His books﴾, that is, the Gospel (al-Injil). It was recited also as "and His books (kutubihi)," meaning the Torah, the Psalms and the Gospel.

His saying: ﴿and she was among the devout (al-qanitin)﴾. If it is asked: how did He say "min al-qanitin" (masculine plural) and not "min al-qanitat" (feminine plural)? We say: Abu al-'Abbas Tha'lab said its meaning is: she was from a people who are devout (qanitin). Qunut is obedience, as we have explained. It is also said that her qunut here is her prayer between the Maghrib and the 'Isha' prayers, and this too is the act of the devout according to this view, and Allah knows best.
